headline: Semis lost double digits while equal-weight beat the index — this is an AI margin call, not a recession trade, but MOVE just stopped being the all-clear.
summary: The S&P fell 3.7% to 6,910 and the Nasdaq 100 fell 5.6% to 25,029, but the damage was violently concentrated: SMH -10.6%, SOXX -10.5%, NVDA -14.0% (now -43.4% in a month and at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range), MU -13.9%, AMD -13.2%, AVGO -12.2%, TSM -9.5%, ASML -6.6%. The offshore mirror is worse: EWT -10.9% (-31.4% on the month), EWY -8.4%, Taiwan's TAIEX -4.4% with a 1m z of -3.11. Volatility went from elevated to regime: VIX +26.2% to 35.89 (z=4.62, acceleration z=+2.63), VIX3M 30.94, and VIX/VIX3M at 1.16 (+10.2% today, 100th percentile). Backwardation is not just present, it is deepening — that is the accelerating-and-bad print of the day.

What actually changed versus yesterday is twofold. First, the selling became differentiated. Yesterday every index printed the same -2%; today equal-weight RSP/SPY rose 1.7% (+7.3% on the month, z=3.5, 100th percentile), IWM/SPY +0.8%, XRT/SPY +2.3%, XHB/SPY +2.4%, KRE/SPY +2.4%, and SPW fell only 2.0% against NDX -5.6%. Software is being separated from silicon: IGV/SMH +6.7% in a day, +17.2% in a month at z=2.40. Second, and less comfortable, bond volatility defected. MOVE +10.7% to 106.31, now +10.8% on the month and +44.8% over three — yesterday's single most reassuring print is gone. Treasuries still worked (TLT +1.4%, IEF +0.9%, 10y -3bp to 5.04%, 2y -4bp to 4.76%), but they are now working with a rising vol-of-rates, and 3m10y flattened another 10bp today to 60bp (1m z=-1.00).

The funding channel keeps leaking in the same three places. Credit: HY OAS +5bp to 3.52, CCC +8bp to 13.61 (+326bp over three months), BBB 1.17 and IG 0.94 — all four at the 100th percentile of the year — while HYG/IEF fell another 1.2% (z=-1.61) and the HYG ETF itself only gave up 0.3%. Collateral: gold -4.0% to 3,539 (0th percentile, -14.7% on the month, z=-3.22), silver -7.3% to 41.08, platinum -4.6%, GDX -5.0%, with gold/silver at 86.15, +19.2% monthly at z=2.81 — the signature of forced sales, not a macro call. Copper -2.8% (-16.5% on the month), COPX -5.0% (-27.8%), FCX -6.4%. EM: USDBRL +0.9% to 5.9335, still +18.1% on the month at z=5.03 with acceleration 3.94, EWZ -32.9% monthly, USDMXN +1.3%, CEW -3.1%, AUDJPY -4.1%. Crypto is the purest leverage read and it broke 60k: BTC 59,004 (-27.4% monthly), ETH 1,624 (-31.9%), MSTR -9.7% to 77.80 (-49.3%).

The offsets are entirely disinflationary and entirely intact. Ten-year breakevens 2.15 (0th percentile, -22bp on the month, z=-1.49), five-year 2.18, gasoline -20.5% and Brent -17.4% over a month. That rebate is showing up in the consumer tape even on a 3.7% index day: WMT +1.5%, COST +0.8%, HD +0.7%, MCD +0.3% (+11.0% on the month), UNH +2.8%, DHI +2.0%, XLP +0.7%. Labour has not cracked — claims 203k, JOLTS 7,523 (+4.6%), unemployment 4.1%. The problem is the price of money: the 10y real yield is 2.88%, 94th percentile and 27% above its 200-day, with breakevens at zero percentile. That is passive tightening into a deleveraging. Risk regime -23 from -19; credit & vol composite -64, rates -51, dollar -58, against an inflation composite of 54 and a growth pulse of -15. Trade the dispersion, not the index: own the disinflation beneficiaries and duration, short the leverage.

good.text: Breadth refuses to confirm the index. RSP/SPY +1.7% to a 100th-percentile reading (+7.3% monthly, z=3.5, acc +1.73), IWM/SPY +0.8%, XRT/SPY +2.3%, XHB/SPY +2.4%; equal-weight SPW -2.0% versus NDX -5.6%. A one-theme unwind, not a market-wide liquidation.
Duration is doing its job: TLT +1.4% (acc z +0.58), IEF +0.9%, LQD +0.6%, 10y -3bp to 5.04%, 2y -4bp to 4.76%, 5y -8bp on the month. The hedge is paying when equities fall.

Disinflation is a hard rebate to the consumer and a permission slip for the Fed: 10y breakevens 2.15 at the 0th percentile (-22bp monthly), 5y 2.18, RBOB -20.5% and Brent -17.4% over a month, DBC -12.5%.
The defensive consumer complex is up on a -3.7% day: WMT +1.5%, COST +0.8%, HD +0.7%, MCD +0.3% (+11.0% monthly), XLP +0.7% with 1m relative strength +16.4%; UPS +8.3% and TGT +9.6% on the month.
India is the only equity market accelerating upward: INDA +1.7% today, +11.9% monthly at z=2.68 with acceleration 2.30, relative strength +25.4% vs the S&P; Sensex +12.4% on the month.
The real economy has not cracked: initial claims 203k, continuing 1.763m, unemployment 4.1%, JOLTS 7,523 (+4.6%), retail sales still +4.7% ytd, industrial production +0.99%.

bad.text: Volatility is now a regime, and it is accelerating: VIX +26.2% to 35.89 (z=4.62, acc +2.63), VIX3M +14.5% to 30.94, VIX/VIX3M 1.16 at the 100th percentile. Deepening backwardation on day two is dealers short gamma, not a one-day panic.

Bond volatility defected: MOVE +10.7% to 106.31 (+44.8% over three months) just as the 10y real yield sits at 2.88% (94th percentile, 27% above its 200-day) and 3m10y flattened 10bp today to 60bp (z=-1.00). Passive tightening with a rising vol-of-rates.

The AI complex is in outright capitulation: SMH -10.6%, SOXX -10.5%, NVDA -14.0% (-43.4% monthly, 0th percentile), MU -13.9%, AMD -13.2%, AVGO -12.2%, TSM -9.5%, EWT -10.9%. SMH/SPY -19.5% on the month at z=-3.10.

Credit keeps grinding wider at the highs of the year: HY 3.52 (+19bp monthly), CCC 13.61 (+326bp over three months), BBB 1.17 (z=1.11), IG 0.94 (z=1.04) — all at the 100th percentile — with HYG/IEF -1.2% at z=-1.61 while HYG itself only fell 0.3%.

Metals are being sold as collateral, not as a view: gold -4.0% to 3,539 (0th percentile), silver -7.3%, platinum -4.6%, GDX -5.0%, GDXJ -5.3%, copper -2.8%, COPX -5.0%, FCX -6.4%. Gold/silver 86.15, +19.2% monthly at z=2.81 and the 100th percentile.

EM and crypto are the leverage tell: USDBRL +18.1% on the month (z=5.03, acc 3.94), EWZ -32.9%, USDMXN at the 100th percentile, CEW -3.1%, AUDJPY -4.1%; BTC through 59,004 (-27.4%), ETH -31.9%, MSTR -49.3%, COIN -42.4%.

trades.name: Software over semiconductors
trades.line: Long IGV / short SMH: the AI unwind hits silicon first
trades.expr: Buy IGV, short an equal dollar amount of SMH. Size 1x each leg; rebalance weekly to stay dollar-neutral.
trades.thesis: The capex-funded part of AI is being repriced while the software layer that consumes it is not. IGV/SMH has gone +17.2% in a month (z=2.40, acceleration +0.75) and is still only in the 55th percentile of its own range after a -26% year — plenty of room before the ratio is crowded. Semis carry the inventory, the Taiwan/Korea FX beta and the hardware capex risk; software carries none of them.
trades.trigger: IGV/SMH +6.7% in a single session. SMH -10.6% and SMH/SPY -19.5% on the month at z=-3.10, versus IGV -4.6% with relative strength already turning up (+1m rs -5.6% but state turning_up). NVDA -14%, MU -13.9%, AVGO -12.2% on the day.
trades.stop: IGV/SMH back below its level of two weeks ago, i.e. the ratio giving back 8% — that means the selling has rotated from chips into enterprise software budgets, which is a different and worse story.
trades.target: A further 12% on the pair as semis mean-revert toward their 200-day gap of -23.6%.

trades.name: Short high beta, own the disinflation consumer
trades.line: Long XLP / short SPHB: the rebate trade with no leverage
trades.expr: Long XLP, short SPHB dollar-for-dollar. Express the tail via 1-month SPHB puts if you want convexity into the vol regime.
trades.thesis: Gasoline -20.5% and Brent -17.4% in a month with 10y breakevens at the 0th percentile is a direct income transfer to the low-end consumer, and the tape is already paying for it. High beta is the funding side of every levered book being cut: SPHB/SPLV -21.0% in a month at z=-3.21 and only the 5.6th percentile of its year.
trades.trigger: On a -3.7% index day XLP rose 0.7% with 1m relative strength +16.4%, while SPHB fell 7.1%. WMT +1.5%, COST +0.8%, HD +0.7% against ARKK -6.8% and IPO -6.5%.
trades.stop: A 6% loss on the pair, which would require oil to re-accelerate (Brent back above its 200-day) or VIX to collapse under 20 and high beta to be bid back.
trades.target: 10% on the pair as the deleveraging runs its course.

trades.name: Long the long end
trades.line: Buy TLT: real yields 94th pctile, breakevens 0th pctile
trades.expr: Buy TLT outright; alternatively long Mar TY/US futures. Scale in on any back-up above 5.10% on the 10y.
trades.thesis: The 10y real yield at 2.88% sits at the 94th percentile and 27% above its 200-day while 10y breakevens print 2.15 at the 0th percentile of the year. That combination is passive tightening into a -15 growth pulse and an accelerating equity deleveraging. The Fed's permission slip is already written in the inflation swaps market.
trades.trigger: TLT +1.4% today with acceleration z=+0.58, IEF +0.9%, 10y -3bp to 5.04% and 2y -4bp to 4.76% on a day equities fell 3.7%. Duration is trading as a hedge again, and 3m10y flattened 10bp.
trades.stop: 10y back above 5.20% / TLT -4%. A failure of bonds to rally on a 3%+ equity down day — with MOVE already +10.7% — would mean this is a supply/funding problem, not a growth problem.

trades.name: India over the EM index
trades.line: Long INDA / short EEM: the only EM accelerating up
trades.expr: Long INDA, short EEM dollar-neutral. INDA is the cleanest expression because EEM's weight is Taiwan/Korea semis plus China.
trades.thesis: EEM is a levered semiconductor and China bet dressed as diversification: Taiwan and Korea drove EEM -15.3% on the month (z=-3.11). India is the opposite — oil importer, domestically funded, a direct beneficiary of Brent -17.4%, and the rupee is strengthening with USDINR -1.5% on the month (z=-1.60) while every other EM cross is breaking.
trades.trigger: INDA +1.7% today to +11.9% on the month (z=2.68, acceleration 2.30, relative strength +25.4%), while EEM -5.1% and EEM/SPY -5.1% monthly at the 0th percentile. EWT -10.9%, EWY -8.4% on the same session.
trades.stop: 5% loss on the pair; or USDINR breaking back above its 200-day, which would mean India has joined the EM funding squeeze that has hit BRL and MXN.

trades.name: Short credit beta against Treasuries
trades.line: Short HYG vs long IEF: the ETF is lying about the index
trades.expr: Short HYG, long IEF dollar-for-dollar — a clean spread-duration short with the rate leg neutralised.
trades.thesis: Every cash spread is at the 100th percentile of the year and still widening, while the ETF has barely moved. HY 3.52, BBB 1.17 (z=1.11), IG 0.94 (z=1.04), CCC 13.61 after +326bp over three months. CCC leading by that margin is the classic sequencing into a default cycle, and with VIX at 35.89 the hedging bid for HY protection has not even started.
trades.trigger: HY +5bp, CCC +8bp, IG +1bp today while HYG fell only 0.3%. HYG/IEF -1.2% at z=-1.61 and rolling over; BKLN -0.2% despite a 0.7% monthly gain that now looks stale.
trades.stop: 2.5% loss on the pair — i.e. HY spreads back inside 3.25 with VIX under 22. A genuine vol collapse makes this the wrong side.
trades.target: 3.5% on the pair, consistent with HY at 4.00 and the 10y toward 4.85%.

trades.name: Natural gas, the one commodity bid
trades.line: Long natgas: +16% today, +35.9% on the month, 26th pctile
trades.expr: Long front-month Henry Hub futures (roll to Jan/Feb), or UNG for an unlevered book. Half size given 16% daily range.
trades.thesis: Natgas is the single commodity with upward acceleration in a complex that is being liquidated: DBC -12.5%, copper -16.5%, gold -14.7% on the month. It is a domestic, weather- and power-demand story uncorrelated to the AI equity unwind, and it still sits at only the 26th percentile of its 52-week range despite the move — this is not a crowded long.
trades.trigger: NATGAS +16.0% today, +17.4% on the week and +35.9% on the month, z=1.81 with acceleration +1.39 and trend turning up, 27.5% above its 200-day.
trades.stop: A 12% drawdown from here, which would mark the move as weather noise rather than a storage story.
trades.target: 18% — roughly the top of the 52-week range.

trades.name: Buy the gold collateral call
trades.line: Long GLD into forced liquidation: 0th pctile, z=-3.22
trades.expr: Start a scaled long in GLD (one third now, add on a 3% further flush). Prefer GLD to GDX until gold stops falling — GDX/GOLD is still -7.4% on the month.
trades.thesis: Gold is not falling on a macro view, it is being sold to meet margin. Gold/silver at 86.15 — +19.2% in a month, z=2.81, 100th percentile — is the textbook fingerprint of liquidation, and those episodes end abruptly. Meanwhile the fundamental case is improving: 10y breakevens at the 0th percentile and a -15 growth pulse argue the Fed cuts into a real yield of 2.88%.
trades.trigger: Gold -4.0% to 3,539, a 1m z of -3.22 at the 0th percentile of the 52-week range and -20.5% below its 200-day, on a day equities fell 3.7% and VIX rose 26%. That non-correlation is the exhaustion signature, not the hedge failing.
trades.stop: 6% below entry, or gold/silver pushing through 90 — that would mean the collateral unwind is still in progress and the sequence has further to run.
